source: Reference video transcribed and timed with ffmpeg/whisper; 220s vertical explainer.
note: The contract is derived from this video, so it must validate. If a change to causal_story.py makes this fixture fail, the change has drifted away from the reference.

observed.hook_type: Opens with a bold promise framing: an authority tried to solve a problem and accidentally made it far worse, explicitly stated to be explained in the simplest possible terms ('like you are five'), immediately setting a curiosity gap.
observed.story_pattern: Numbered chronological steps (step one through step six) walk through a cause-and-effect chain: problem introduced, well-meaning solution deployed, unintended exploitation emerges, authority reacts, situation ends worse than the start, then abstracts into a named general principle with multiple parallel examples.
observed.recurring_characters: Simple round-headed stick figures represent everyone — the authority figures (marked by uniform hats), the ordinary population (marked by regional dress), and a lone narrator-avatar figure who appears solo to deliver lessons directly to camera with pointing and expressive gestures.
observed.location_reuse: A rotating set of era-appropriate backdrops (grand official building, interior office, marketplace street, back-alley slum) reused to anchor each narrative beat, alternating with plain single-color backgrounds for the direct-address and principle moments.
observed.visual_composition: Hand-drawn cartoon illustrations in warm sepia/amber tones; wide establishing scenes for story beats, schematic diagrams (branching multiplier chart, before/after cause arrows, world map) for abstract points, and tight centered close-ups of the avatar for lesson delivery.
observed.on_screen_text: A single bold word (the current keyword being spoken) sits centered on screen as a karaoke-style caption, changing continuously in sync with narration rather than showing full sentences.
observed.narrator_tone: Conversational, wry and explanatory; builds suspense with short punchy declaratives and deadpan reversals, treating the audience as smart but needing things spelled out plainly.
observed.humour_and_interrupts: Comedy comes from dramatic irony and understatement — the logical-sounding plan repeatedly backfiring — plus visual gags like an overwhelming swarm and mock-'sensible' bureaucratic reactions.
observed.reveal_placement: The core twist (the exploit backfiring) lands around the one-third to halfway mark, followed by a later reveal naming the general principle, then rapid-fire parallel real-world examples to reinforce it.
observed.ending_callback: Closes by circling back to the opening theme, poses a reflective rhetorical question tying the abstract lesson to the viewer's own life, then delivers a sponsor plug and a call-to-action to try an app.

story.title: The Cobra Effect
story.start_state: Delhi has a wild cobra population that is killing people

hook.line: How the British Empire tried to solve a problem and accidentally made it much worse.

steps.label: 1800 colonial India
steps.situation: Delhi is full of venomous cobras, in the streets and in the homes, killing people.

steps.label: The bounty
steps.situation: The colonial government pays a cash bounty for every dead cobra brought in.

steps.label: Problem solved
steps.situation: Simple, logical, efficient. Kill a cobra, get paid, fewer cobras.

steps.label: Except
steps.situation: Except the problem is not solved.

steps.label: Incentives beat intentions
steps.situation: Give people a financial incentive and they will find a way to maximize it, whether you intended that or not.

steps.label: You can breed them
steps.situation: People realize they do not have to hunt cobras. They can breed them at home, in boxes, for almost nothing.

steps.label: Cobra farms
steps.situation: Cobra farms appear, thousands of snakes bred specifically to be killed for British money.

steps.label: The bounty is cancelled
steps.situation: The government sees impossible payment volumes, investigates, finds the farms and cancels the bounty.

steps.label: Released
steps.situation: The farms are now worthless, so the farmers release thousands of captive-bred cobras into the streets.

steps.label: Worse than before
steps.situation: The cobra population is now significantly larger than when the government started trying to fix it.

steps.label: The pattern is everywhere
steps.situation: The same shape repeats wherever a measure replaces the goal it was meant to track.

steps.label: What are the cobra farms?
steps.situation: Next time someone offers a simple solution to a complicated problem, ask what the cobra farms are.

parallel_cases.solution: a bounty paid per rat tail
parallel_cases.result: rat farms, then release, then more rats than before
